teks: $ZEC I’d wait before opening a short on ZEC. As long as price remains stuck in this tight range, I don’t see any clear direction. I want to see a convincing breakdown below the trendline, followed by confirmation. Shorting too early here only means taking unnecessary risks. The goal isn’t to predict the move, but to wait for the market to confirm it.

I could tell you that the bottom is here, right now. But I’d be pulling your leg, because no one can know for certain where the low will be. If you’re an investor, these levels may present interesting opportunities for spot accumulation, whilst keeping capital available for any even deeper pullbacks. When it comes to trading, however, it’s a completely different story. Wait for a range to form, for the market to build up liquidity, and for clear triggers to emerge. You don’t have to guess where the bottom is. You have to wait for the price to offer you an edge. In recent days, forcing trades without a clear structure has done nothing but wipe out the portfolios of X’s reckless traders. Patience costs you nothing. Pointless stop-losses, on the other hand, do.

I hope you found this message useful. Personally, I’ve hardly touched altcoins at all, apart from one or two positions over the last two weeks. I’ve remained calm and patient, taken very few stop-losses and, above all, preserved my capital. And that was one of the best decisions I could have made in this market environment. As I’ve been telling you for days, if we don’t first observe Bitcoin and establish a clear direction, there’s no point in looking for opportunities elsewhere in the market. Trading doesn’t mean always being in the market. Sometimes the best trade is the one you decide not to make.

As I’ve been saying for days now in my previous tweets, a low doesn’t form overnight. There are two possibilities: 1. A sharp sell-off, with falls of as much as 20–30 per cent in a single day, followed by a strong market reaction. 2. A slow formation of the low, through a trading range, accumulation, deviations and retests of key levels. A low takes time, requires a structure and, above all, needs confirmation. At the moment, I see nothing that would allow me to say that the low has been reached. I could tell you what you want to hear, but that’s not how I trade. There’s no point in guessing the low. We need to recognise it when the market gives us confirmation. Patience. The price will give us the answers.

Around 3 BILLION dollars have been liquidated in the last few hours. I still don’t understand all this rush to trade. What’s the point? To give money away to the market? Personally, I’ve only tried one trade on $BTC – a long position near 60k, which was stopped out around 58k. One stop. End of story. It was an interesting level; it was worth a go. It didn’t work out – never mind. But that’s the difference between trading and gambling. Constantly jumping in, opening positions every hour, every minute, trying to recoup every loss – that doesn’t make you a trader. It means slowly destroying your capital. And I don’t even need to prove it to you. You’ve seen it with your own eyes over the last few days. Trading isn’t a race to see who can open the most trades. It’s a race to see who can preserve their capital long enough to capitalise on the real opportunities. Learn to sit tight. It’s one of the most difficult and important skills in this profession.
